value.body: A mine planning engineer decides where and in what order a mine will dig — the shape of the pit or the underground layout, the schedule, and the equipment needed — so that the mine meets its targets safely. Mining companies, mining contractors and mining consultancies hire them. Most days are spent at a computer with geology models and survey data, with regular visits to the mine to check plans against reality.

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Site office at the mine, or a corporate planning office

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start in mine operations and move to planning after some site experience; some companies and consultancies take freshers directly into planning cells. Training in a mine-planning package helps.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working with block and geological models

value.title: At a glance
items: Site experience makes planning work more realistic and is valued.
Common next roles: senior planner, planning head, mining consultant.
Mining plans and their approvals are regulated, so documentation is a large part of the work.
